narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimates a 63.5% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. This is a risk-based prediction, not a certainty: the model still sees roughly a one-in-three chance you would pass, but it judged the risk high enough to deny admission.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing. Your third-year decile was 1, far below the accepted-student average of 5.79, and this was the most influential reason pushing the prediction toward failure. The next most important factor was your LSAT score of 36, slightly below the accepted average of 37.18; despite being below average, it actually pushed toward passing rather than failure. Your first-year decile of 2, compared with an accepted average of 6, was the third most important factor and also pushed toward failure.

To move forward, ask admissions what would most strengthen a future application, seek academic advising, and consider focused LSAT preparation or a retake if feasible. You should also discuss any context or extenuating circumstances that affected your grades, and apply to programs where your profile is a better fit.
